boundary: memsys5, SQLite's own arena allocator, under the engine
title: Engine-internal memory-safety defects in SQLite 3.22.0, measured against a nested allocator
note: Sibling of capi-repros, not an extension of it: those 19 rows are pointer-lifetime defects in host BINDINGS over the C API, and that corpus records SQLite's engine-internal defects as out of scope. These 43 are engine-internal. Five further R2 fuzz-diff images (fz01, fz03, fz04, fz05, fz07) are collected and carry a host-ASan signature but no derived trigger, so they are not cases here; deriving them needs the 3.43.1 fuzz corpus re-extracted for db-by-sql pairing. Eight more entries in the collection are diagnostics rather than defects -- five baseline probes and three allocator demonstrators -- and stay in the port. The memsys5 boundary is the point: a sub-allocation is the address arena+i*atom, so it inherits the whole arena's bounds, and both a use-after-free and an overflow that stays inside the arena are in bounds for a capability machine.
